title: On-call & Incident Response: Rotations, Runbooks, Postmortems, Game Days, and Comms
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

This page consolidates Redwood Inference's standard on-call and incident response practices: incident lifecycle, runbook structure, postmortem expectations, rotation schedules, game day exercises, and status page / customer communication templates. It is intended for engineers, SREs, incident commanders, and support leads. Follow these procedures for any production-impacting incident.

Goals and scope
- Keep customer-facing impact minimal (meet SLOs & SLAs).
- Clear ownership and fast remediation for production incidents.
- Preserve learning via high-quality postmortems and follow-ups.

SLOs and alert thresholds (examples)
| Service | P95 latency | Error rate | Pager threshold |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| api-generation | 800ms | >1% 5m | Pager if 3+ alerts in 5m |
| embedding-service | 250ms | >0.5% 10m | Pager if sustained errors for 10m |

Incident severity taxonomy
- Sev 1 (SEV-1): Customer-facing outage or complete service degradation. Pager and immediate IC.
- Sev 2 (SEV-2): Major degradation with significant customer impact. Pager and on-call response.
- Sev 3 (SEV-3): Partial impact or internal issue with limited customer effect. Slack escalation.
- Sev 4 (SEV-4): Informational or scheduled maintenance. No pager.

Incident response lifecycle (high level)
1. Detect: automated alert or customer report.
2. Triage: on-call responder assesses impact and assigns severity.
3. Mobilize: Incident Commander (IC) is declared and channels created (incident Slack + Zoom).
4. Mitigate: apply runbook or mitigation play.
5. Communicate: internal and external communications per templates below.
6. Resolve: service restored or acceptable mitigation.
7. Postmortem: document timeline, root cause, action items.
8. Follow-up: verify mitigations and close action items.

Roles & responsibilities
- Primary on-call: first responder, initial triage and temporary mitigations.
- Secondary on-call: backup; escalates to IC if primary cannot mitigate.
- Incident Commander (IC): coordinates response, owns communications and timeline.
- Subject Matter Experts (SMEs): service owners and engineers called in for deep fixes.
- Communications lead: prepares status updates and customer-facing messages.

On-call rotations and expectations
- Team rotations: 1-week rotation for infra and runtime teams.
- Handover: each shift must update the on-call log in /confluence/eng-sre/oncall-handover with current incidents, mitigation status, and follow-up actions.
- Coverage hours: weekdays 24/7 coverage with on-call escalation policy; weekends have reduced escalation (primary -> secondary -> pager duty leads).
- Escalation policy: If primary doesn't acknowledge within 10 minutes, page secondary; after 15 additional minutes, escalate to IC on-call.

Runbook structure (standard template)
- Title: short service name + play.
- Symptoms: observable alerts and logs.
- Severity: recommended severity for the play.
- Preconditions: access and perms needed (grafana, alerts, ssh, k8s).
- Quick mitigations: step-by-step actions to reduce impact.
- Full remediation steps: detailed commands, config changes, or deployment steps.
- Rollback steps: how to undo changes safely.
- Post-incident checks: verification commands and dashboards to watch.
- Owners and contacts: pager team and SMEs.

Example quick mitigation snippet (plain commands)
1) Redirect traffic to fallback cluster: kubectl patch svc api --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/selector/cluster","value":"api-fallback"}]'
2) Temporarily increase replicas: kubectl scale deploy api --replicas=10 -n prod
3) Clear problematic queue: redis-cli -h redis.prod flushdb (only if safe)

Postmortem expectations
- Timeline: minute-by-minute timeline from detection to resolve.
- Impact statement: which customers/features were affected and for how long.
- Root cause analysis: concise technical cause and contributing factors.
- Corrective actions: prioritized list with owners and ETA (JIRA links).
- Preventative actions: systemic changes to reduce recurrence.
- Severity review and SLO impact calculation (tokens, requests, revenue if applicable).
- Quality bar: postmortem must be published within 72 hours for SEV-1/2 and within 7 days for SEV-3.

Game days and exercises
- Frequency: quarterly team-wide game days; focused tabletop drills monthly for high-risk subsystems.
- Objectives: validate on-call processes, runbooks, and status page tooling; measure MTTR.
- Typical scenario: KV cache incoherence under load, causing 40% error rate on generation service.
- Post-exercise: update runbooks and measure improvement in response time and triage accuracy.

Status page and customer communications
- Channels: status.redwood.ai (public), status API, email for major incidents, customer Slack/contacts for enterprise customers.
- Update cadence: initial ack within 30 minutes for SEV-1/2, then updates every 60 minutes until resolution.

Customer-facing status template (example)
- Title: [Incident] Degraded text-generation API - partial outage
- Impact: We are experiencing a partial outage affecting text-generation endpoints in us-west-2. Customers may see increased latency and errors.
- Current status: Investigating.
- Next update: In 60 minutes or sooner.
- Affected services: /v1/generate, streaming API
- Workaround: Retry requests or use synchronous endpoint <link>.

Internal announcement template (Slack + PagerDuty)
- Subject: SEV-{level} - {short description}
- Body: Detection time, brief impact, IC name, main mitigation in progress, channel link, action items.

Runbook review & maintenance cadence
- Owners must review runbooks quarterly and after any related incident or game day.
- Major changes require at least one reviewer and a short changelog entry in the runbook header.

Incident metrics and reporting
- Required metrics to track per incident: detection_time, ack_time, mitigation_time, resolution_time, customer_impact_estimate (units). Keep these as fields in the postmortem.
- Weekly SRE review: summary of incidents, MTTR, top recurring causes, and closed action items.

Appendix: Postmortem checklist (SEV-1/2)
1. Create incident page and timeline.
2. Declare IC and create incident channel.
3. Post initial status to status page and internal Slack.
4. Capture key logs and metrics (request traces, error rates).
5. Apply mitigation and document exact steps.
6. Verify service stability for at least 30 minutes.
7. Draft and publish postmortem within 72 hours.

Appendix: Customer email template (after resolution)
Subject: Incident summary - {date} - {brief title}
Body:
Hello {CustomerName},

On {date} we experienced an incident affecting {service}. The issue was detected at {time} UTC and resolved by {time} UTC.
Impact: {short description of features/customers affected and duration}.
Root cause: {concise root cause}.
Resolution: {what we changed / rolled out}.
Follow-up actions: {list of actions and ETA}.
If you have questions or need an impact report for your team, contact {support@redwood.ai} or your account owner.

Thanks,
Redwood Inference Reliability Team
